questions.question:
Which of the following type of unemployment is there in rural areas?

I. Seasonal Unemployment

II. Disguised Unemployment
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Seasonal unemployment** is prevalent in **rural areas** due to the dependence on **agriculture,** which is a **seasonal activity.**
 
• **Disguised unemployment** is also common in** rural areas**, where more people are engaged in **agricultural** activities than required, resulting in **low productivity.**
 
• Seasonal unemployment is more prevalent in areas where there is a dependence on natural resources, such as** forestry, fisheries, and mining.**
 
• Disguised unemployment is a situation where **people appear to be employed**, but their contribution to the economy is **minimal.**
 
• Structural unemployment and **frictional unemployment** are not common in rural areas, as there is l**ess job mobility **and fewer industries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Structural unemployment is caused by a** mismatch **between the** skills of workers** and the** requirements of employers.**
 
• Frictional unemployment is a **temporary unemployment **situation that occurs when people are in the **process of changing jobs.**
 
• Rural areas are also affected by **cyclical unemployment**, which is caused by **economic fluctuations.**
 
• Disguised unemployment is prevalent in the** informal sector**, where people are engaged in activities that are not recognized by the **government or** are not registered.

questions.question: A bike rider covers 100 km at a speed of 75 km/h. At what speed does the rider have to drive for the next one hour to get an average speed of 90 km/h?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total time of the journey = (100 ÷ 75) + 1 = 4/3 + 1 = 7/3 hours.

Total distance for an average speed of 90 km/h = 90 × (7/3) = 210 km.

Distance left to be covered in the next 1 hour = 210 − 100 = 110 km.

Required speed = Distance ÷ Time = 110 ÷ 1 = 110 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 110 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b4f721231f1fca62f9cabd79045cd78e1ab54f716f32f36319ca9be7032f5a7a.png] 

**Given:**

Initial Distance (D₁) = 100 km

Initial Speed (S₁) = 75 km/h

Time for second part (T₂) = 1 hour

Target Average Speed = 90 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Time (T₁) = D₁ ÷ S₁ = 100 ÷ 75 = 4/3 hours

⇒ Total Time = T₁ + T₂ = 4/3 + 1 = 7/3 hours

⇒ Total Distance = Average Speed × Total Time = 90 × (7/3) = 210 km

⇒ Distance covered in second part (D₂) = Total Distance − D₁ = 210 − 100 = 110 km

⇒ Required Speed (S₂) = D₂ ÷ T₂ = 110 ÷ 1 = 110 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 110 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

Average speed is the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. It is not always the arithmetic mean of given speeds unless the time intervals are perfectly equal.

When Distances Are Equal

If a person travels equal distances at speeds S₁ and S₂, the average speed is given by the harmonic mean formula: (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. Conversely, to convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: In a college canteen, food items were collected to serve 96 students for 5 days. But due to new admissions, 64 more students joined. Now, for how many days the food items would last?
questions.solution:
**Given Data:**

Initial number of students = 96

Food for = 5 days

Additional students = 64

**Concept:**

The number of students and the number of days are inversely proportional.

**Calculation:**

Total number of students now = Initial number of students + Additional students

⇒ Total students = 96 + 64 = 160

Number of days food will last = (Initial number of students × Initial number of days) / Total number of students

⇒ Days = (96 × 5) / 160 = 3 days

**Therefore, the food items would last for 3 days.**
